advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test planting an nvme serial that contains the well-formed requested volume id as a non-token substring (e.g. serial `xvol0ddd3333eeee4444fy` on a wrong device) and assert the anchored match does NOT resolve to it, distinguishing the anchored match from the old substring behavior.
evidence: Commit body: 'The nvme serial match is anchored to a whole token in the identify page rather than any substring of it. Defense in depth behind the shape guard'

Named violating input: a well-formed id `vol-0ddd3333eeee4444f` requested against a host where a wrong device's serial embeds it as a substring token, e.g. serial `xvol0ddd3333eeee4444fy` on nvme0n1 — the old substring `grep -qi` would match it, the anchored form must not; no test in the file plants such a serial.
ABSENCE: the two AC4 seed-the-defect tests drop only markers `REFUSE-DEGENERATE-VOLUME-ID` and `REFUSE-EMPTY-FILESYSTEM-UUID`; the anchoring change has no marker and no dedicated test.
advisory.finding: The anchored whole-token nvme-serial match added at user_data.sh:84-85 (replacing the plain substring `grep -qi "$vol_nodash"`) is newly-introduced behavior with no test that exercises it. Every existing test is satisfied by the shape guard (require_well_formed_volume_id) firing first or by the exact-serial happy path; none plant a device whose serial CONTAINS a well-formed requested volume id as a non-token substring, which is the only input class that distinguishes the anchored match from the old substring match. A regression that reverts line 85 back to the plain substring form would leave the entire suite green.
scenarios: A future edit reverts the anchored regex to a plain substring match; suite stays green while the substring-collision defect the anchoring was added to prevent returns.
An nvme identify page emits the requested id embedded inside a longer alphanumeric token on the wrong device.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test that writes a serial like `pad{GOOD_SERIAL}pad` (id as an internal substring of a longer token) onto nvme0n1 while removing/altering nvme1n1's exact serial, request GOOD_VOLUME, and assert it does not resolve to nvme0n1 (returncode != 0 or empty stdout). Optionally add a seed-back variant that reverts the regex to a plain substring and asserts the collision then resolves, mirroring the AC4 pattern.

evidence: infra/terraform/user_data.sh:53 `grep -qiE '^vol([0-9a-f]{8}|[0-9a-f]{17})$'` — validation runs on the already-de-dashed value, so dash placement in the raw arg is not constrained
advisory.finding: `require_well_formed_volume_id` validates the DE-DASHED string (`vol_nodash=$(echo "$1" | tr -d '-')`), so `tr -d '-'` strips dashes from anywhere in the argument, not just the canonical single `vol-` separator; an input like `v-o-l-0ddd3333eeee4444f` or `vol--0ddd...` collapses to an accepted shape and is treated as well-formed.
advisory.suggested_fix: Validate `$1` directly against `^vol-([0-9a-f]{8}|[0-9a-f]{17})$` (dash included, anchored) before the `tr -d '-'` normalization, then de-dash for the serial match.
